<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, I will first obtain the 13C NMR spectrum of the compound using the carbon_nmr_spectra tool. Then I will retrieve typical carbon chemical shift ranges for carbonyl carbons with retrieve_carbon_shifts. By comparing the observed carbon signals to the carbonyl shift range (generally ~190–220 ppm), I can count how many distinct carbonyl carbons are present, which corresponds to the number of C=O groups.</thought>
<action>carbon_nmr_spectra</action>
